title: SAIL: Test-Time Scaling for In-Context Imitation Learning with VLM
abstract: arXiv:2603.08269v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: In-context imitation learning allows robots to acquire skills from demonstrations, yet one-shot trajectory generation remains fragile under environmental variation. We propose SAIL, a framework that reframes robot imitation as an iterative refinement problem capable of scaling with test-time compute. SAIL utilizes Monte Carlo Tree Search, where each node is a complete trajectory and edges correspond to trajectory refinements. The process is guided by three core components: an automated archive of successful trajectories for contextually relevant retrieval, a vision language model-based scoring mechanism for trajectory evaluation, and a step-level feedback that provides trajectory-aligned scores for iterative refinement. Experiments across six diverse manipulation tasks in simulation and real-world validation clearly demonstrate that increasing test-time compute consistently improves success rates, achieving up to 95% on complex

translated_title: SAIL：基于视觉语言模型的上下文模仿学习的测试时扩展
translated_abstract: 上下文模仿学习使机器人能够从演示中习得技能，然而一次性轨迹生成在环境变化下仍然十分脆弱。我们提出了SAIL，一个将机器人模仿学习重新构建为可随测试时计算量扩展的迭代优化问题的框架。SAIL利用蒙特卡洛树搜索，其中每个节点代表一条完整轨迹，边对应轨迹的优化改进。该过程由三个核心组件引导：用于上下文相关检索的成功轨迹自动化存档、基于视觉语言模型的轨迹评估评分机制，以及为迭代优化提供与轨迹对齐评分的步级反馈。在六个多样化操作任务的仿真实验和真实世界验证中，结果清楚地表明增加测试时计算量能够持续提升成功率，在复杂任务上最高达到95%。
tldr: SAIL框架将机器人模仿学习重构为迭代优化问题，通过蒙特卡洛树搜索结合成功轨迹自动存档、视觉语言模型评分机制和步级反馈，实现了测试时计算量的有效扩展，在六个操作任务上将成功率最高提升至95%。
